response.text:
### (1) Hypotheses

Let

\[
\mu_1=\text{mean weight loss for low-calorie diet},
\]
\[
\mu_2=\text{mean weight loss for low-fat diet},
\]
\[
\mu_3=\text{mean weight loss for low-carbohydrate diet},
\]
\[
\mu_4=\text{mean weight loss for control}.
\]

The one-way ANOVA hypotheses are

\[
H_0:\mu_1=\mu_2=\mu_3=\mu_4
\]

versus

\[
H_a:\text{not all four means are equal}.
\]

Equivalently, at least one diet has a different population mean weight loss.

---

### (2) ANOVA table

There are \(k=4\) groups with \(n_i=4\) subjects each, so

\[
N=16.
\]

Degrees of freedom:

\[
df_{\text{between}}=k-1=3,
\]

\[
df_{\text{within}}=N-k=12,
\]

\[
df_{\text{total}}=N-1=15.
\]

We are given

\[
SS_{\text{Total}}=114.4.
\]

Let

\[
SS_{\text{Diet}}=4\sum_{i=1}^4(\bar y_i-\bar y_{\cdot\cdot})^2
\]

be the between-diet sum of squares. Then

\[
SS_{\text{Error}}=114.4-SS_{\text{Diet}}.
\]

Thus the ANOVA table is

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & df & SS & MS & F \\
\hline
\text{Diet} & 3 & SS_{\text{Diet}} & \dfrac{SS_{\text{Diet}}}{3}
& \dfrac{SS_{\text{Diet}}/3}{(114.4-SS_{\text{Diet}})/12} \\
\hline
\text{Error} & 12 & 114.4-SS_{\text{Diet}}
& \dfrac{114.4-SS_{\text{Diet}}}{12} & \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 15 & 114.4 & & \\
\end{array}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
F=\frac{SS_{\text{Diet}}/3}{SS_{\text{Error}}/12}.
\]

---

### (3) Do we reject \(H_0\)?

From the information given, we **cannot determine** whether to reject \(H_0\). The total sum of squares alone,

\[
SS_{\text{Total}}=114.4,
\]

does not determine how much variability is due to differences among diet means versus random within-diet variability.

To make the decision, we need either the raw data, the four sample means, or \(SS_{\text{Diet}}\) / \(SS_{\text{Error}}\).

At significance level \(\alpha=0.05\), the rejection rule would be

\[
F>F_{0.95,3,12}\approx 3.49.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\frac{SS_{\text{Diet}}/3}{(114.4-SS_{\text{Diet}})/12}>3.49.
\]

This is the same as requiring approximately

\[
SS_{\text{Diet}}>53.3.
\]

But since \(SS_{\text{Diet}}\) is not given, the rejection decision cannot be made from the stated information alone.
